title: HOT-SIDE MEMORY: oxide gain-cell tiers in the backside-power carrier wafer (carrier-last), plus at most 4 tiers in the logic BEOL
status_reason: The energy-per-bit step survives every correction (~11x vs HBM delivered at SM-local placement, 5.5x worst case). The system claim halves, from ~190 to ~90 W/GPU, because traffic share tracks capacity and the planning case drops to 1 b/cell: RTN, cross-temperature and 1e-4 tail-leakage terms are unmeasured, and the tail alone makes it refresh-light rather than refresh-free. Cost rises from $1.36-3.55 to $4.6-12/GB. Bond-first is replaced by a carrier-last flow to sidestep the FATAL backside-overlay objection and In/Ga/Zn exposure, which only a BSPDN foundry can finally prove. No objection kills the physics.

revised_verdicts.possible: Yes at 1 b/cell: refresh-light, with the 1e-4-tail refresh at ~3.6 s (105 C) and ~1.4 s (125 C), ~225x rarer than Si. 2 b/cell is conditional on a 1e-4 RTN quantile <=30 mV, cross-temperature residual <=10 mV, tail leakage <=7.5 aA at 105 C and drift <=20 mV in a >=600 mV window, none of which is measured yet. No law is violated. Backside overlay and contamination are engineering risks, sidestepped by the carrier-last flow.
revised_verdicts.profitable: STEP CHANGE IF IT WORKS: energy per bit moved, ~10x lower than HBM (0.37 vs 3.95 pJ/b delivered; 5.5-15x depending on placement), down from ~12x. ~90 W saved per 2028-30 backside-power GPU at the 16 x 1 b planning case (48 W at 8 x 1 b, ~170 W if 2 b works), down from ~190 W. Not a cost step: $4.6-12/GB, 3-8x DDR5 cost, 1-3x below the HBM4 price.
revised_verdicts.doable: PROVABLE WITH $1M: partly. The cell question (drift, RTN, cross-temperature, 1e-4 tail, real-bond hydrogen) is answered for ~$240k by M11. Logic shift on 22FDX plus carrier proxies (IPD, CSAM voids, VPD-ICPMS) fit in $1.00M by M22. Production backside overlay, killer-defect density, foundry materials acceptance and a named BSPDN partner need the raise.

revised_experiment: Gate A+ (M2-11, ~$240k), the decisive test. Purdue/GT vertical channel-all-around (>=0.01 um2 read gate) 2T0C coupons in IGZO, In-poor IGZO, IGO and ZTO, with single vs series write gates and -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold. Each split is measured after the post-bond heat/H sequence AND a real D2O-labelled 350-400 C fusion bond (cap chips, SIMS H/D). Measurements on >=1e5 cells per split: drift sigma at 1/10/100 s at 85/105/125 C; write-at-T1/read-at-T2 maps (dT +/-30 K) with in-row references; RTN from >=100 reads ~1 s apart plus fast reads at 1 us-1 ms; write-FET Vt/SS and the directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile; top-tier dVt after bonding. PASS 1 b (planning): drift <=75 mV, RTN 1e-4 quantile <=100 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, bonded dVt <=10 mV. PASS 2 b (upside): drift <=20 mV in a >=600 mV window, cross-temperature residual <=10 mV, RTN quantile <=30 mV, tail <=7.5 aA at 105 C. Then Gate B (M18) on 22FDX logic: RO <=1%, Vt <=10 mV under 2 tiers, 1,000 h bake, placement sigma <=10 mV in <=3 loops/<=60 ns. Then Gate C (M22): carrier emulation with in-plane distortion (film-stress maps, FEM, wafer-geometry IPD vs a blank reference) replacing bow; CSAM on 20 bonded pairs; VPD-ICPMS In/Ga/Zn <=1e10 at/cm2; heater <=1 K at 10 W/mm2 with 10% via fill. M0-3 includes the capacity-indexed trace and placement study and claim reading of US 12,666,958 and US 2025/0167193. Total plan $1.00M (experiments $677k) in 24 months.

responses.response: Valid against the bond-first flow (today's BSPDN order: carrier bonded before thinning and backside litho). With ~100 MPa net tier stress and 10% die-scale non-uniformity, 3-10 nm of intrafield distortion uses up the <10 nm backside-overlay budget. Bow was the wrong Gate C metric. Two answers. (1) Baseline becomes a CARRIER-LAST flow. The logic wafer goes through thinning and backside litho on an inorganic IR-release temporary Si carrier (EVG IR LayerRelease class: inorganic release layer, front-end and fusion/hybrid-bond compatible, vendor claim, logged). The backside is then moved to a second temporary carrier, the front is released, and the memory wafer is hybrid-bonded at 1.5 um pitch, which tolerates ~100-300 nm of alignment error. The memory wafer never sees backside litho, so carrier-induced overlay goes to zero. Cost in the model: +$400/wafer and 1% logic scrap from the two temporary bond/debond cycles. (2) Bond-first stays only as a conditional option: stress-neutral tier films (|net| <=10-20 MPa gives ~0.3-2 nm by the reviewer's own scaling) plus dummy-filled scribe and periphery. The field-repeating part of the fingerprint is correctable by intrafield high-order correction, so only the non-repeating residual counts.
responses.action: Carrier-last is the baseline flow (model: carrier_last_usd $400, p_kill_temp_bond 1%). Gate C metric changes from bow to in-plane distortion: film-stress maps of patterned vs blanket tiers, FEM, and wafer-geometry IPD of SOI bonded to a tier coupon vs a blank-carrier reference. Bond-first is kept only if the residual is <=1-2 nm (3 sigma) at a BSPDN partner (imec, CEA-Leti or Intel); that is a raise milestone, and kill criterion 6 is rewritten.

responses.response: Correct. W2W bonding has no known-good-die screen, so only carrier sites under the ~38 good logic dies ship, not all 64 gross sites. That alone is x1.68. Model re-run with GB/wafer = 38 x GB/die x 0.9, together with PROC-03, the 28 nm carrier, ECC and the carrier-last adder. 16 x 2 b goes from $1.36 to $4.61/GB, 16 x 1 b (planning) from $2.71 to $9.22/GB, and 8 x 1 b from $3.55 to $11.87/GB. That is 3-8x DDR5 cost and 1-3x below the HBM4 price. Per GPU the near tier costs ~$420-650 against ~$790-1,500 of 5-year value at ~$16.4 per W saved, so it remains net positive. The 'DDR5-like dollars' line is withdrawn. A D2W known-good-die route is the revival, at the cost of losing the free carrier slot.
responses.action: Cost claim downgraded from $1.36-3.55/GB to $4.6-12/GB: a premium near tier, not cheap bits. Section 9 of the model now uses good_logic_dies = 38. The step-change axis (energy) is unaffected.

responses.response: Accepted. A sequential vertical 2T0C tier needs >=5-6 patterned, registered levels: write WL, read gate, channel/via, write BL, read BL/SL and SN contact. That is ~88 masks for 16 tiers. At ~$100 per level all-in, a tier costs ~$550 rather than $300, and the 16-tier adder becomes $12,350/wafer with the 28 nm carrier and the carrier-last steps. The 16 chained registrations cost yield, which binning absorbs, and money, which it does not. No EUV is added (ArFi single exposure), but mask count is no longer a selling point.
responses.action: tier_usd raised from 300 to 550; the 16 x 2 b cost moves to $4.61/GB, already included in PROC-02. Revival condition logged: self-aligned multi-tier patterning with <=3 litho levels per tier (NAND-style), or a foundry quote of <=$5k/wafer for a 16-tier stack. Mask count is listed as a cost, not a benefit, in sections 2 and 8.

responses.response: Valid that voids were not counted, but 33% overstates the problem. With a 2.5 mm void radius each particle kills ~11 cm2 of 800 mm2 dies, so <=1% loss needs <=0.0009/cm2, about one particle per wafer pair. The 0.05/cm2 is CELL-WAFER FOUNDRY's merchant pre-bond figure. Production BSPDN already fusion-bonds a heavily processed logic BEOL surface (15+ CMP'd levels) at a yield the foundries accept. A processed carrier adds a second processed surface, not the first. The carrier is also the cheap side: it can be Surfscan-inspected and then re-cleaned, re-CMP'd or scrapped ($8-12k) before it meets a $30k logic wafer. A thick CMP-last bond oxide removes tier topography. Planning incremental density is 0.001/cm2, giving 1.1% void loss. Total logic scrap is 2.7% ($21/die) with 4 BEOL tiers and the carrier-last steps, or 2.3% carrier-only.
responses.action: Void term added to model section 8 (void_D_cm2 0.001, R 2.5 mm). The flow gets pre-bond carrier inspection with re-clean or reject. The seed adds CSAM plus Surfscan on 20 fusion-bonded 200 mm pairs with tier-emulating topography ($45k) to calibrate void size vs particle count. A university cannot reach the fab-grade rate, so the production rate is a foundry/raise milestone.

responses.response: Valid for bond-first: the carrier would ride through grind, CMP, nano-TSV etch, metal and forming gas on shared 18A/A16 backside tools while the logic silicon is exposed from the back. Ga and In are acceptors in Si and Zn is a deep-level killer. The carrier-last flow adopted for PROC-01 also removes most of this exposure. The memory wafer arrives only after all backside litho, etch and metallization, and sees only the hybrid-bond, anneal, debond and bump steps, which run on advanced-packaging lines that already handle more materials than FEOL. Added on top: full SiN/Al2O3 encapsulation of the tiers, 2-3 mm edge exclusion with no oxide semiconductor near the bevel, and a bevel etch and clean before the carrier leaves the memory line.
responses.action: Seed adds VPD-ICPMS/TXRF ($15k, commercial lab) on encapsulated, bevel-cleaned coupons after backside-sequence emulation. Target: In/Ga/Zn <=1e10 at/cm2 on all exposed surfaces. New kill line: if this fails, bond-first is dead and the carrier host rests on carrier-last. A foundry materials-review sign-off is a raise milestone.

responses.response: Correct on the dossier's own numbers. At the 1e-4 quantile (3.72 sigma) with SS 95 mV/dec, write-FET sigma_Vt of 30/50/100 mV gives 15x/91x/8,217x, not 3x. That is a 105 C tail of 13 aA and a 125 C tail of 46 aA at 50 mV, against ceilings of 7.5 aA (2 b, 1 s) and 22.5 aA (1 b, 1 s). Three answers. (1) Series or double-length write gate (top-up I-12627). In a vertical cell it costs no footprint, only a 0.20 to 0.24 um taller tier. A cell then leaks only if both segments are outliers, so the 1e-4 pair quantile sits at z = 2.33 (independent) to 2.96 (rho 0.5): 17-36x at 50 mV before any stack-effect credit. (2) Hold bias -0.5 to -0.7 V buys ~127x for subthreshold-limited cells, which makes the single FET 0.7x. If leakage is not subthreshold-limited, the Vt-sigma mapping does not apply in the first place. (3) The planning value is now 25x. That gives a 1-b refresh of 3.6 s at 105 C and 1.4 s at 125 C (1 b passes 125 C at 12.5 aA), and a 2-b refresh of 0.64 s and 0.25 s. Unmitigated 91x gives 0.24 s (2 b, 105 C) and 0.49 s (1 b, 125 C).
responses.action: tail_leak_mult raised from 3 to 25, with the 91x unmitigated case shown in model section 11. Refresh claim downgraded from 'refresh-free, ~6,400x fewer refreshes' (typical cell) to 'refresh-light': ~225x fewer than Si at 105 C for 1 b (1e-4 tail) and ~40x for 2 b. Refresh power for 78 GB is ~0.2-0.5 W vs 1.8-7.2 W for Si. Gate A adds write-FET Vt/SS distributions on >=1e5 cells, a directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile at 105/125 C, single vs series write-gate splits and -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold splits.

responses.response: Accepted: RTN in the read FET is a missing term that neither references nor write-verify cancel. Single-trap dVt = q/(Cox A) at EOT 4 nm. For the planar 40 nm gate (0.0016 um2), eta = 11.6 mV and P(err) ~3e-3, or 9e-2 with 3x percolation: 2 b is dead in planar cells. For the vertical channel-all-around read FET (0.01-0.015 um2), eta = 1.2-1.9 mV, giving P(err) 4e-22 to 5e-15, or 5e-8 to 1e-5 with 3x percolation. So 2 b is plausible only in vertical cells and only if percolation stays at <=3x. Search found no IGZO-specific RTN amplitude data (logged), so this is unmeasured. Budget change: half the raw-BER budget (5e-5) is reserved for RTN, and the Gaussian terms get the rest. Cells that show inconsistent verify reads are flagged and remapped (1% capacity budget). 1 b, with a 300 mV half-spacing, is insensitive to RTN.
responses.action: Model: rtn_ber_share 0.5, which moves the 2-b allowed drift from 24 to 20 mV. Vertical channel-all-around read FETs with >=0.01 um2 gate area become a design rule. Gate A adds >=100 repeated reads ~1 s apart, plus fast reads at 1 us-1 ms spacing, on >=1e5 cells at 105 C. 2 b needs the 1e-4 RTN quantile <=30 mV (eta <=3.3 mV, P(>60 mV) = 1e-8); 1 b needs <=100 mV.

responses.response: Valid: Gate A annealed unbonded coupons, so it never saw the ~2-5e14 H2O/cm2 that a 350-400 C oxide-oxide bond releases within ~1 um of the top tier. 0.1% of that acting as channel donors would shift Vt by 30-70 mV, far over the 10 mV budget. Fix: a real bond moves into Gate A. Small Si cap chips with 0.5-1 um of product-like bonding oxide are plasma-activated, hydrated with D2O and fusion-bonded over the array area of tier coupons, leaving the pads exposed, then annealed at 350-400 C for 2 h. The deuterium label separates bond-plane hydrogen from bulk hydrogen in SIMS (DOE nanocenter). The split also runs with and without a 10-20 nm ALD Al2O3 barrier and a SiCN bond dielectric.
responses.action: Gate A gains a bonded split (+$25k, M6-11); the Gate A date moves from M10 to M11 (2027-11-30). Pass: top-tier dVt <=10 mV and drift within the unbonded split's class. Fail: kill criterion 1 is evaluated on the bonded split, not the unbonded one.

responses.response: Mostly accepted. kT/C on 0.15 fF is 5.9-6.1 mV rms at 105-125 C and is re-sampled on every write. Because verify reads after WWL falls, it captures both kT/C and the kickback spread, so the final placement is a verify-truncated distribution rather than a kT/C draw. A +/-10 mV acceptance window (5.8 mV rms) plus 8 mV verify noise gives 9.9 mV, so the 10 mV placement sigma holds. One try lands within window 90% of the time, and three tries 99.9%. The timing point is right: 3 loops x (5 ns write + 10-15 ns sense) is ~45-80 ns, not 20 ns. Writes are 20% of traffic and posted through logic-side SRAM, and only ~0.13% of one tier's subarrays are active at peak bandwidth, so read latency and bandwidth are unaffected. 1 b needs no verify loop.
responses.action: Model: t_write_ns 60. The 2-b write is quoted as ~60 ns posted, and the write energy is 0.54 pJ/b at the port including the global WBL. Gate B (22FDX readout with tiers) measures placement sigma <=10 mV within <=3 iterations in <=60 ns at 105 C. Probe-card coupons cannot time ns loops.

responses.response: Correct. 16 tiers x 2.5e10 cells with 64 x 256 subarrays needs 6.3e9 SAs and 3.1e9 WL drivers: 0.13 um2 and 0.26 um2 each, or ~24x the carrier area. Redesigned floorplan, re-run in model section 11(a): 8,192-cell rows, a 64-cell local RBL behind an oxide segment switch, and a 4,096-cell in-tier global RBL with one via per tier to a Si 16:1 tier mux and a shared 2-b SA in the carrier. That gives 9.1 um2 per WL driver and 146 um2 per SA, or 50% of the carrier area in 28 nm-class CMOS (3 um2 drivers, 25 um2 SA+mux). The tier-select device is now Si in the carrier, not oxide. The remaining oxide segment switch runs in deep triode at >=1.5 V overdrive: a 50 mV Vt sigma moves Ron ~3%, and with Ron <=10% of the read-FET resistance that is <1 mV equivalent. Per-segment reference rows cancel the common mode. Costs: tier efficiency 0.50 to 0.45; global RBL/WBL of 126 fF; read 0.087 to 0.121 pJ/b; 2-b write 0.134 to 0.54 pJ/b; mix 0.21 pJ/b at the port; sense residual 8 to 10 mV; carrier CMOS $1,800 to $2,800 (28 nm-class). A 65 nm carrier fits only ~4-5 tiers.
responses.action: Model: array_eff_carrier 0.45, cells_per_row 8192, c_gbl_fF 126, sigma_read 10 mV, carrier_cmos_usd 2800, E_oxide_refresh_fJ 200. Capacity at 16 x 2 b drops from 89 to 78 GB/die. M0-3 design work delivers a carrier floorplan with SA and driver counts per mm2 and SPICE of the hierarchical RBL with an extracted 16-tier via. The 2-b row page is 2 KB with read-modify-write.

responses.response: Valid. a-IGZO Vt moves ~-17 mV/K (long-channel display TFT; unmeasured for 40 nm ALD channels). A 25-30 K swing between write and read is 0.4-0.5 V of common mode, and a 5% cell-to-cell tempco spread leaves 21-26 mV, the whole 2-b budget. Mitigation: (a) each 2 KB row carries its own three per-level reference cells, written in the same burst (0.04% overhead), so temperature history, drift and tempco are common to data and references; (b) a write-temperature tag per region, plus a rewrite when |T - T_write| > 10 K, holds the residual to 5% x 17 x 10 = 8.5 mV. Rewrite is an internal row cycle. Steady serving rarely trips the rule, but kernel-scale hotspot motion of 20-40 K on ms scales could trip it often over the ~15% hotspot area, which is why 1 b is assigned there (thermal-map bits per cell, delta #4). The residual is modelled as a 10 mV term, which with the RTN reserve takes the 2-b drift allowance to 20 mV. 2 b is not proven until cross-temperature maps exist, so the planning case follows the reviewer's default: 1 b.
responses.action: Model: sigma_xT_mV 10, plan_bits 1. The planning capacity at 16 tiers halves from 157 to 78 GB/GPU, and 2 b becomes an upside. Gate A adds write-at-T1/read-at-T2 maps (dT +/-30 K) on >=1e5 cells with in-row references; 2 b passes only if the residual sigma is <=10 mV. The tempco is measured on 40 nm ALD devices at 25-125 C.

responses.response: Accepted. In decode every resident byte is read each step, so the near tier's traffic share is about its share of resident bytes. The model now indexes share to capacity: additive = C/(C+288), HBM-shrink = C/288, planning = their mean, capped at 0.5. Revised density and delivered energy (0.37 pJ/b): 8 x 1 b (39 GB/GPU) is 13% and 48 W; 16 x 1 b (78 GB, planning) is 24% and 92 W; 16 x 2 b (157 GB) is 45% and 169 W. The 190 W headline belonged to the 16 x 2 b best case. A hot subset, such as skewed MoE expert popularity, shared experts or prefix KV, could raise share above byte share, but that is unproven until traces show it.
responses.action: W/GPU headline downgraded from ~190 W to ~90 W (planning 16 x 1 b; range 48-169 W); model traffic_share() added. The M0-3 trace study must report the bytes-moved share vs resident share on production decode traces (dense and MoE). Kill criterion 8 is re-indexed.

responses.response: Correct: RS(36,32) with 8-bit symbols at raw BER 1e-4 fails 3.6e-6 per codeword (recomputed). The 12.5% cannot also cover random errors. Fix: rows are 2 KB (CIRC-01) and are activated whole, so an inner binary BCH over each 16,384-bit row (m=15) at t=23 uses 345 parity bits (2.1%) and fails at 4.7e-20, below the 2e-19 target. The outer tier-orthogonal RS keeps handling a whole failed tier. Combined overhead is 1.125 x 1.021 = 1.149, against CIRC's 1.32 with a 512-bit BCH. Capacity falls ~2% (not 89 to 76 GB), and reads gain ~20-40 ns of decode latency (~50-80 ns total, still below HBM's ~100+ ns).
responses.action: Model: ecc_overhead 1.149, recomputed in section 11(d). Latency quoted as ~50-80 ns. The controller RTL budget includes a row-BCH decoder. The code choice is revisited once Gate A gives the error-cluster spectrum (per RAW-BER CONTRACT).

responses.response: Valid: 1 mm assumed every byte sits above its consumer. With random placement the mean SM distance on 800 mm2 is ~9 mm, delivered energy 0.71 pJ/b and the ratio 5.5x. Mitigation: SM-local placement is natural for decode. Each GEMV weight tile is read by exactly one SM every step under a fixed tiling, and FlashDecoding-style KV splits give each sequence chunk to one SM. Both can be pinned to the near-tier region above that SM cluster (~0.4-0.9 GB per SM at 39-78 GB/die) with a NUMA-style address map, as spatial accelerators already do for SRAM. The planning case puts 80% of reads at ~1.5 mm and 20% at ~9 mm, a 3 mm mean: 0.37 pJ/b delivered vs 3.95 pJ/b for HBM, ~11x (15x at 1 mm, 5.5x at 9 mm).
responses.action: Model: L_deliver_near_mm 3, with the 1/3/9 mm sweep in section 11(e). The per-bit claim becomes ~10x (5.5-15x). The trace study adds a placement simulation that must show >=80% of near-tier reads within 1-2 mm. Placement or addressing claims go into the IP list as defensive publication.

responses.response: Accepted; this is the same coupling as CIRC-03. Additive capacity gives 12-35% share, so 45-133 W across 8 x 1 b to 16 x 2 b. The HBM-shrink placement gives 14-50%, so 51-189 W. The planning case (16 x 1 b, mid) is 24% and ~92 W, roughly half of 190 W. Per bit, the gain survives at ~11x. The 5-year value per GPU at ~$16.4/W goes from ~$3,100 to ~$1,500 for 16 x 1 b. That still covers the revised near-tier cost (~$650/GPU) about 2x. HBM-shrink also removes ~2 HBM4 stacks (~$1,150), which would on its own cover the near-tier cost.
responses.action: Same downgrade as CIRC-03: ~190 W becomes ~90 W planning. The decisive trace study runs in M0-3 on production decode traces. It passes the 'hot subset' case only if >=50% of bytes moved come from <=30% of resident bytes; otherwise the capacity-indexed number stands.

responses.response: Valid as worded: Rubin is a front-side-power product, and 'every leading-edge die' is false before ~2028. Corrected premise: backside power puts a bonded carrier on every A16, 18A and 14A-class die. Reported programs exist. Nvidia is reported as TSMC's first A16 customer for Feynman (2028, samples possibly 2027), and OpenAI was earlier reported to have booked A16 capacity (logged; reports, not TSMC confirmations). That window, ~2029-31, is when a carrier product could ship after an 18-24 month demo and a $10-50M development round anyway. The 22 TB/s Rubin-class GPU is kept only as a bandwidth proxy, and HBM bandwidth per GPU rises in later generations. For front-side-power hosts there is a fallback: an SoIC/V-Cache-style face-to-back bond with TSVs through the logic. It works, but it pays for a full extra wafer, so the 'free slot' advantage is lost there. No named program has asked for an active carrier.
responses.action: Section 0 premise reworded, and the watts are quoted against a '2028-30 backside-power accelerator at >=20 TB/s'. Raise gate: a named BSPDN accelerator or foundry contact (A16, 14A or 18A) willing to evaluate a third-party carrier before the Series A. The front-side-power SoIC fallback is added to the scale path.

responses.response: Accepted. The broad claim is barred (Chip Scale Review 2022; imec CMOS 2.0). Binning and SLC/MLC switching are established practice, and TSMC, imec and Samsung each hold more of the stack. A foundry could build the option itself. The red team created narrower but real reductions to practice that a foundry would need and does not yet have published. (1) Carrier-last oxide-memory flow with the bevel/encapsulation contamination package. (2) Bond-interface hydrogen control: a D2O-labelled qualification method plus a barrier and SiCN bond stack with data. (3) Cross-temperature MLC: in-row references, write-temperature tags and a delta-T rewrite rule. (4) RTN screening and remap for gain cells. (5) A Si tier-mux carrier floorplan under oxide tiers. The business case is therefore data, know-how and team toward a JDA or acquisition, not a royalty stream. The founder framing does not kill on business grounds, but the licensing upside is lowered.
responses.action: Claims of US 12,666,958 and US 2025/0167193 are read in M0-3 (within the $40k IP line), before filing. Provisionals are re-ordered to (2), (3), (1), (4), (5). An FTO opinion comes before the raise. Exit thesis: a foundry or memory-maker JDA naming the startup as data and IP owner of the qualification method.

responses.response: Partly refuted, partly accepted. The standalone $1M plan already funds Gate B on real 22FDX dies (logic RO/Vt shift under 2 tiers, 1,000 h bake), which is the reviewer's own second 'change my mind' condition. Only the portfolio-seed variant was Gate-A-only. Accepted: production-scale killer density (<=1.25e-4/cm2), backside overlay on real BSPDN logic and Cu bonding on production wafers cannot be shown in $1M. Seed proxies are added for each foundry risk the reviewers named. Overlay: patterned-vs-blanket tier film-stress maps, FEM and wafer-geometry IPD vs a blank-carrier reference ($20k, folded into carrier emulation, now $130k). Voids: CSAM plus Surfscan on 20 bonded 200 mm pairs ($45k). Contamination: VPD-ICPMS/TXRF ($15k). The budget is rebalanced to $1.00M: sky130 dropped, BEOL post-processing reduced to 2 tiers, contingency 4.3%.
responses.action: Revised plan is $1,000k: salaries 240 + experiments 677 + IP 40 + contingency 43. Gate B on 22FDX stays inside the seed. The data room states plainly which numbers are proxies (IPD, CSAM, VPD) and which are foundry-only (overlay residual, defect density, materials acceptance). PROVABLE stays 'partly'.

responses.response: Valid as a tax, smaller than feared once the vias are sized to the power map. The tier stack is now 3.84 um because of the series-gate cells. Unvia'd it adds 27 K at 10 W/mm2; 3% Cu fill gives 2.9 K and 10% gives 0.93 K. Revised rule: 10% fill over the ~15% hotspot area and 3% elsewhere, giving 0.93 K over hotspots and 0.29 K at the 1 W/mm2 average, for ~1.5% capacity cost. That meets the reviewer's <=1 K line. The 1-D model ignores lateral spreading, so it is an upper bound. The tax is offset: a share of the ~3.5 pJ/b HBM path (PHY and NoC) is dissipated on the GPU die, and the near tier removes most of it from the hottest die. The '89 becomes 44 GB' point is accepted and already covered by the 1-b planning case.
responses.action: Model: via_fill_hot 0.10 and tier_thick 0.24 um. Gate C heater pass tightened to <=1 K at 10 W/mm2 with 10% fill (was <=5 K with 3%). Hotspot regions run 1 b. A perf/W net check (logic clock vs memory-path watts) goes into the M22 data room.
